title: Invariant open complements of saturated closed-set closures
statement: Let $R,V$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $s,t:R\to V$ be flat affine morphisms [def-weil-flat-morphism, pqf-def-affine-morphism], and let $e:V\to R$ satisfy $s\circ e=t\circ e=\mathrm{id}_V$. For a subset $A\subseteq|V|$ set $\sigma(A)=t(s^{-1}(A))$, and call a subset $F$ invariant when $s^{-1}(F)=t^{-1}(F)$. Assume $\sigma(A)$ is invariant for every subset $A\subseteq|V|$. Let $H\subseteq|V|$ be a quasi-compact open [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and $K\subseteq H$ an invariant subset closed under generalization, meaning $y\in K$ and $y\in\overline{\{y'\}}$ imply $y'\in K$. Put $Z=|V|\setminus H$, $T=\sigma(Z)$ and $B=\overline T$. Then $Z\subseteq T$, $K\cap T=\varnothing$, and every point $y\in B$ is the specialization of some point $y'\in T$, that is, $y\in\overline{\{y'\}}$. Moreover $s^{-1}(B)=t^{-1}(B)$ and $K\cap B=\varnothing$. Consequently $W=|V|\setminus B$ is an invariant open subset with $K\subseteq W\subseteq H$.

source.place: Tag 0APB (lemma-second-observation), proof: Z, T, closure of T and its open complement; abstracted to the stated source-target saturation axioms, with affine s,t as in the descent application.

proof.text: For $z\in Z$, the point $e(z)$ has $s(e(z))=t(e(z))=z$, so $z\in T$. If $x\in K\cap T$, choose $r$ with $t(r)=x$ and $s(r)\in Z$. Invariance of $K$ gives $s(r)\in K$, contradicting $K\subseteq H$. Thus $Z\subseteq T$ and $K\cap T=\varnothing$. The saturation hypothesis applied to $Z$ gives $s^{-1}(T)=t^{-1}(T)$.

source.place: Tag 0APB, lemma-second-observation, proof: saturation T of the closed complement, closure invariance, and its open complement

proof.text: Let C=s⁻¹(Z), a closed subset of R since s is continuous and H is open. Construct I=Scheme.IdealSheafData.vanishingIdeal C and i=I.subschemeι using [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-closed-subscheme]. Mathlib gives QuasiCompact i directly for this subscheme inclusion. The affine morphism t is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Composition of quasi-compact morphisms, in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], gives QuasiCompact (i ≫ t). The range formula for subschemeι and the range-of-composition identity identify its image with T.

source.place: Tag 0APB, lemma-second-observation, proof: saturation T of the closed complement, closure invariance, and its open complement

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-picard-closure-specialization] to the quasi-compact morphism $j:D\to V$ of step 2. Since its image is $T$, each $y\in B=\overline T$ admits $d\in D$ such that $y'=j(d)\in T$ and $y\in\overline{\{y'\}}$. This proves the required assertion about every closure point.

source.place: Tag 0APB, lemma-second-observation, proof: saturation T of the closed complement, closure invariance, and its open complement

proof.text: Let $r\in R$ with $s(r)\in B$. Step 3 gives $y'\in T$ generalizing $s(r)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] for the flat map $s$, there is $r'$ generalizing $r$ with $s(r')=y'$. Invariance of $T$ gives $t(r')\in T$. Continuity of $t$ sends $r'\leadsto r$ to $t(r')\leadsto t(r)$: equivalently, preimages of closed sets are closed. Therefore $t(r)\in B$. Conversely, if $t(r)\in B$, choose $y'\in T$ generalizing $t(r)$ by step 3 and apply the same cited lifting lemma to the flat map $t$. The lift $r'$ has $t(r')\in T$, hence $s(r')\in T$ by invariance; continuity of $s$ gives $s(r)\in B$. These are the two inclusions $s^{-1}(B)=t^{-1}(B)$.

source.place: Tag 0APB, lemma-second-observation, proof: saturation T of the closed complement, closure invariance, and its open complement

proof.text: If $y\in K\cap B$, step 3 gives $y'\in T$ with $y\in\overline{\{y'\}}$. The assumed generalization stability of $K$ gives $y'\in K$, contradicting $K\cap T=\varnothing$ from step 1. Hence $K\cap B=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0APB, lemma-second-observation, proof: saturation T of the closed complement, closure invariance, and its open complement

proof.text: The complement $W=|V|\setminus B$ is open because $B$ is closed. Taking complements in the equality of step 4 gives $s^{-1}(W)=t^{-1}(W)$. Step 5 gives $K\subseteq W$. Since $Z\subseteq T\subseteq B$, taking complements gives $W\subseteq|V|\setminus Z=H$.

lean.statement: theorem flat_relation_invariant_open_complement {R V : Scheme.{u}} (s t : R ⟶ V) [Flat s] [Flat t] [IsAffineHom s] [IsAffineHom t] (e : V ⟶ R) (hes : e ≫ s = 𝟙 V) (het : e ≫ t = 𝟙 V) (hsat : ∀ A : Set V, s ⁻¹' (t '' (s ⁻¹' A)) = t ⁻¹' (t '' (s ⁻¹' A))) (H : V.Opens) [CompactSpace H] (K : Set V) (hKH : K ⊆ (H : Set V)) (hK : s ⁻¹' K = t ⁻¹' K) (hgen : StableUnderGeneralization K) : (H : Set V)ᶜ ⊆ t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ) ∧ K ∩ (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)) = ∅ ∧ (∀ y ∈ closure (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)), ∃ y' ∈ t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ), y ∈ closure ({y'} : Set V)) ∧ s ⁻¹' closure (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)) = t ⁻¹' closure (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)) ∧ K ∩ closure (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)) = ∅ ∧ IsOpen (closure (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)))ᶜ ∧ s ⁻¹' (closure (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)))ᶜ = t ⁻¹' (closure (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)))ᶜ ∧ K ⊆ (closure (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)))ᶜ ∧ (closure (t '' (s ⁻¹' (H : Set V)ᶜ)))ᶜ ⊆ (H : Set V)
